context.why: This package's whole design rests on one namespace never affecting another. Payment libraries model subscriptions genuinely differently, so there is deliberately no common interface across them and no neutral component — a second backend gets a namespace beside the first rather than underneath it. That separation is currently an intention expressed in the structure of the code. This story makes it a guarantee a test holds. There is only one real payment backend, so the second namespace is a fixture inside the test suite: the property under test is that two contributions are independent of each other, and that needs two contributions and nothing else.

spec_sections: User Story 5 - A second backend leaves the first alone
prior_decisions: D2 — URL names are grouped under one application namespace, app_name = 'payments', and every name carries its own namespace slug. Collision is meant to be impossible by construction; this story is the test that says so.
D1 — every surface reads available_contributions(). A second contribution is added to CONTRIBUTIONS for the duration of a test, not by editing the shipped tuple.

Three earlier stories hit real limits with in-process setting overrides and each recorded what it found (D9, D10, D14). Read those entries in decisions.md before choosing your mechanism, and say which you chose and why.
context.conventions: CONSTITUTION.md Article X — a test fixture application inside tests/ has no source module to mirror, so if it needs declaring, declare it under [tool.forge.conformance] non-mirror-paths in pyproject.toml rather than leaving the structure check to guess. Article XVI — assert rendered output, never the presence of a class name.

acceptance.given_when_then: Given the test suite, when a second namespace is defined in it — a minimal installed application to gate on, and a contribution declared against it — then it registers through exactly the same mechanism as the shipped one, with no special case anywhere in mvp_payments/.

Given only the first namespace's backend installed, when its navigation entries, its card and its page addresses are captured, and then the second namespace is added alongside it, then all three are identical to what they were. Assert against the rendered navigation and the rendered card region, not against the menu objects.

Given both namespaces available, when each namespace's page addresses are resolved, then neither resolves to the other's page, and no two declared contributions share a URL name. The naming scheme already carries the namespace slug, so this is expected to pass without production change.

Given the README's namespaces section, when it is read, then it says that a second namespace is added beside the first and changes nothing about it. docs/namespaces.md already documents how one is added; keep it true.
